candidateModels.rationale: Matches every piece of collected evidence: the dominant formula's sole input (source_ref), the bulk writer's own comment ('preserve existing packet_key when source_ref already exists'), the co-equal independent treatment of sourceRevision/workspaceRevision/representationRevision in every consumer traced, and the Qdrant projection's explicit cross-representation stability requirement (which SOURCE_COORDINATE_PACKET naturally satisfies since source_ref does not vary by representation).

Would require rename survival. No producer or consumer implements or expects this; stableFileId (UUIDv7, already frozen) already fills this exact role as a separate identity axis -- packet_key is not wired to it anywhere found.

identity-resolution.ts explicitly ranks symbol_version_id ABOVE packet_key in its precedence chain -- packet_key is a fallback used precisely when symbol-version granularity is unavailable, not a proxy for it.
No byte-span/occurrence input to the dominant formula; TreeNodeOccurrenceV1 (a separate, already-frozen contract) owns this grain instead.

No append-only behavior found anywhere -- both traced writers produce at most one row per source_ref (one mutates in place via onConflictDoUpdate on packetId, the other no-ops via ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on packet_key); atlas_packets is not an append-only revision log for this axis.

Evidence converges cleanly on SOURCE_COORDINATE_PACKET without conflicting signals from any traced consumer -- the one genuine open question (B, rename) is an absence of evidence, not a conflict between two evidenced expectations.

renameSemantics: Packet identity is scoped to a source_ref coordinate. A rename (source_ref A -> B for the same logical file) legitimately produces a different packet_key under this model -- this is not a defect relative to the SOURCE_COORDINATE_PACKET contract, though it does mean packet_key cannot answer 'is this the same file that moved', which is stableFileId's job, a deliberately separate axis.
revisionSemantics: packet_key does NOT change when sourceRevision, workspaceRevision, or representationRevision change -- those are tracked as independent, co-equal fields on the same identity envelope everywhere this pass found packet_key used. This is the model's central design point: one packet_key per source coordinate, revisions layered alongside it, never folded in.
aliasSemantics: LEGACY_ENCODING_COMPATIBILITY only, confirmed by both prior gates and this one -- atlas_packet_identity_aliases exists to reconcile a historical wrong-prefix bug (ace:packet: vs packet:), not to provide rename continuity, revision continuity, or cross-scheme compatibility beyond that one bug. No consumer traced this pass expands that contract.

collisionPolicy.currentBehavior: SILENT_SKIP -- INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (packet_key) DO NOTHING against a live UNIQUE(packet_key) constraint. A genuine 12-hex truncation collision between two distinct source_refs causes the second file to silently receive no atlas_packets row at all, with no error, no receipt, and no log entry inspected this pass.
collisionPolicy.requiredBehaviorRationale: Inferred from this repo's own existing fail-closed identity discipline, not invented: stable-file-identity-mint-v1.ts's own stated rule is 'Ambiguity (>1 existing row for what should be a unique scope) throws rather than picking arbitrarily' -- the same standard should apply to a genuine packet_key collision between two distinct source_refs. A complementary, not mutually exclusive, mitigation is FULL_DIGEST_REQUIRED (drop the 12-hex truncation in favor of a full-width digest, which reduces collision probability by many orders of magnitude but does not by itself add receipt/rejection behavior for the residual risk).
collisionPolicy.defectRationale: SILENT_SKIP does not match COLLISION_RECEIPT_AND_REJECT, HARD_FAIL_IDENTITY_COLLISION, SECONDARY_DISAMBIGUATION, or FULL_DIGEST_REQUIRED -- it is the one behavior explicitly not on the acceptable list. The prior gate's birthday-bound estimate (~1-in-165,000 at current scale, ~1-in-14,000 at a projected 200k rows) means this defect is currently low-probability but not zero, and grows with corpus size under the present formula.

lifecycleResultRationale: Every traced consumer and both traced writers agree, without contradiction, on the same model: packet_key identifies a source_ref coordinate, is stable across revision/representation/cluster/graph-reprojection/process-restart, and is NOT expected to survive rename or track symbol-version/revision granularity. The only open axis (B, rename) is an absence of evidence rather than conflicting evidence, and does not block calling the model PROVEN -- it blocks nothing about the model itself, only confirms rename-instability is an accepted, uncontested consequence of the model rather than an unaddressed requirement.
encodingStatusRationale: The lifecycle MODEL is proven and the current 12-hex truncated-hash formula's INPUT semantics (source_ref only) correctly implement that model -- the defect is narrowly in the WRITE-TIME COLLISION HANDLING (silent DO NOTHING), not in what the formula identifies. This is deliberately reported separately from lifecycleResult per the gate's mandatory A/B split.
sharedBuilderReadinessRationale: Lifecycle is PROVEN, but current encoding does NOT satisfy the contract (collision policy defect) -- extracting the current formula verbatim into a permanent shared module would canonize the silent-skip defect alongside the correct source-coordinate semantics. Per instruction, no builder is created in this gate regardless.

futureSharedBuilderRequiredContract.inputs: source_ref only (confirmed sufficient for the SOURCE_COORDINATE_PACKET model; no revision/representation/cluster input should ever be added, per the proven co-equal-axis design)
futureSharedBuilderRequiredContract.output: a packet_key string -- digest width increased from 12 hex (48 bits) to at least full sha256 (or another collision-resistant width with an explicit, documented birthday-bound justification for the target corpus size) to satisfy FULL_DIGEST_REQUIRED as a complementary mitigation
futureSharedBuilderRequiredContract.collisionBehavior: COLLISION_RECEIPT_AND_REJECT -- on a write attempt whose computed key already exists in atlas_packets under a DIFFERENT source_ref, the writer must reject the write and emit an explicit collision receipt (matching this repo's existing evidence-receipt discipline), never silently skip
futureSharedBuilderRequiredContract.normalization: not audited this pass whether source_ref normalization (case, path separators, leading/trailing slashes) is applied consistently across the traced writers -- flagged as an open question for whoever implements the shared builder, not resolved here
futureSharedBuilderRequiredContract.revisionBehavior: MUST NOT be an input to the key formula -- sourceRevision/workspaceRevision/representationRevision remain co-equal sibling fields, never folded into packet_key, per the proven model
futureSharedBuilderRequiredContract.renameBehavior: MUST NOT attempt rename continuity -- that is stableFileId's role; a shared packet-key builder that tried to survive rename would violate the proven SOURCE_COORDINATE_PACKET model, not fix a defect
